Quari: The Monk Who Punches You With A Glacier
Quari, The Astral Pilgrim: Growth, Glaciers, and Grit

Quari is a 5-star Legendary hero from the Astral Dwarfs family, representing the Ice (Blue) element. As a Monk running at Average speed, Quari fits the role of a "bruiser support"—a hero who deals significant damage while simultaneously buffing the team's long-term survivability. Released in late 2024, he introduced the concept of "Growth" (permanent stat increases) to the Astral family, making him a cornerstone for players who prefer winning through attrition and overwhelming power rather than quick, glass-cannon snipes.

Quari’s design is distinct, featuring a flowing beard and headpiece that many players have noted draws inspiration from Eastern aesthetic traditions. He looks like a warrior-monk who has traveled the galaxy (or the "Astral Plane") and returned with ancient wisdom—and a very large, glowing weapon. The cool blues and golds of his armor fit the Ice element perfectly, giving him a serene yet imposing presence.
Quari's stats are well-rounded, ensuring he can perform his hybrid role effectively.

Quari is a fantastic "anchor" hero. If you are struggling to keep your team alive while dealing damage, he solves both problems. Level him immediately and pair him with a standard healer to become invincible.

You might overlook him for faster heroes, but don't sleep on the Growth. +200 Attack/Defense is like having an extra troop level on everyone. For Mythic Titans or long War fights, that stat differential wins games.
Players loved his distinct look, calling him the "Lovechild of Darkfeather and Sparklight."
Some users found him "flaky" or inconsistent because if the DoT is cleansed, he loses value. Others swore by him as a "Consolation Prize" that turned out to be a main prize.

Quari is the Astral Dwarf who decided that the best way to help his friends is to hit his enemies so hard they leak life force. He is a master of attrition, slowly tipping the scales of battle in your favor with every turn that passes. While he lacks the instant "I win" button of some Rush heroes, his "Fluvial Path" is a road that inevitably leads to victory if you can walk it long enough.
Bottom line: Let it flow, let it grow.
